title: Fix faux nightshift lighting lasting forever
author: MrMelbert
body:
## About The Pull Request

When updating APCs, night shift does `set_nightshift(!nightshift_disabled)`. 
`nightshift_disabled` is only set to `TRUE` in the event the station is on red alert, meaning during a typical run, night shift would run its course, turn off, and then call `set_nightshift(!FALSE)` / `set_nightshift(TRUE)`.

Additionally, `tick` is not called after an event `end`s - meaning if the event failed to complete its `currentrun`, any unhandled APCs would stay in whatever state.

(I will note, this is realllllyyyy slow. Like, visually. It can only run about 12 APCs at a time before it pauses for next tick.)

changes.text: Night lighting actually goes away when it ends

title: The lightening: minor fix for lighting overlay hard deletes
author: vinylspiders
body:
## About The Pull Request

fixes #98319

```
## REF SEARCH Found /datum/component/overlay_lighting [0x21058116] in list Datums -> /datum/spatial_grid_cell [0x21009cab] -> dynamic_light_sources (list).
## REF SEARCH Found /datum/component/overlay_lighting [0x21058116] in list Datums -> /datum/spatial_grid_cell [0x21009cac] -> dynamic_light_sources (list).
## TESTING: GC: -- [0x21058116] | /datum/component/overlay_lighting was unable to be GC'd -- (ref count of 4)
```

This is the rest of #97967. that got closed as a dupe of #97786, but #97786 only fixed part of it.

The component works out which grid cells to leave from its current range, so changing the range while it's lit leaves it in the cells only the old range reached. burning mobs hit this since the fire light shrinks as the stacks burn down. deleting the light then hard dels the component, and any lumcount read in those cells runtimes on it (`Cannot read null.current_holder`)

#97786 also left a few other ways to end up in the wrong cells:
- switching a light off without moving it kept it in its cells, so it still counted as light
- `set_light_range(0)` turned the light off without cleaning up
- the light picks its first holder before the component is listening, so moving that first holder (a light spawned on the floor, a mob's own light) never moved its cells
- a light taken out of a bag on the same tile it went in on stayed out of the grid

Now the component remembers the cells it registered in and leaves exactly those, clears them first on every re-register like #97967 did, re-registers when its range changes, cleans up when it's switched off, and grabs its first holder once it's listening. Range changes also update the holder's luminosity now, that used to stay at whatever range the light had when it got picked up or switched on. `set_power()` doesn't re-register anymore since nothing reads the stored power, and moving a lit light builds one cell list per step instead of two

Tested and verified to be dead for good now, stupid hard deletes

## Why It's Good For The Game

Hard dels are bad, and shadow walking and the other darkness checks now see lights where they actually are

changes.text: switched off lights no longer count as light for shadow walking and other darkness checks, and lights that move around count where they actually are

title: Adds a balloon warning when ventcrawling into pipes that arn't room temperature.
author: moocowswag
body:
## About The Pull Request


When entering pipes via ventcrawl do_after you will be alerted if the vent feels hot or cold (and in absence of an alert, room temperature)

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0b78d6cf-fd55-46f4-b67d-2633f40112eb

The way it is implemented should give you a warning near where you are already looking so you can easily react within the time it takes for the do_after to complete.

Breathability and pressure remain unknown until you subject yourself to the container. 

## Why It's Good For The Game
Its annoying to have to dance around in pipes waiting for life or atmos or whatever to tick to see if the gas mix is going to kill you, this eliminates the most obvious case of extreme temperatures which often results in long lasting damage or for slimes an instant death.

I thought about doing more cases for breathability and pressure but it would make the balloon alert too large....and to_chat warnings are too annoying to look at and diagnose if its something your controlled mob cares about within the timeframe of the do_after...especially when you could be getting hit while trying to ventcrawl.

That and its more intuitive to be able to tell the temperature of something's contents via initial contact than pressure or gas composition.



An alternative to this pr (or in addition to it) could be to add an alt-right click (or something) functionality to ventcrawlers to allow them to stick their head in to briefly sense contents without having to wait for something to tick or anything.

But I think that would have much more considerations of being able to fully discover if a pipenet is completely safe for you...currently the pr already appropriately telegraphs the main threat of entering a vent and arguably the only threat that should be telegraphed.

I could add more tells like "warm/hot/very hot" but im not sure if that would be too much?

I dont know if its qol or not...for most cases its qol because youre just saving time awkwardly spent dancing in a pipe, for slimes it could be considered balance since cold pipes are a stunlock into effectively an instant kill with no warning (although did we ever want that to begin with?)

changes.text: Ventcrawling critters will now be able to tell if the vent they are entering is uncomfortable temperature.

title: Wounds for robotic limbs (ported from bubberstation and recoded)
author: Fghj240
body:
## About The Pull Request
_ew, the FURRY is porting stuff from a FURRY ERP server!!_

This PR adds wounds for robotic bodyparts, which takes code from skyrat, nova, and bubber. It does not add slash or pierce wounds, only burn and blunt ones, a lot of the mechanics were heavily adjusted including making them weaker overall. 

**Bleeding wounds** aren't coming (for now at least) because I think the idea of a wound just dealing damage over time to you is stupid and chip damage is especially annoying when you can't heal with medicine. Plus, it's a LOT of code and I don't even know if this is gonna get merged so I'm breaking it down.

**Burn wounds** are the metal heating up to a glow. The bodypart takes more damage like a normal burn wound, and you also glow a little while burned. Burns slowly raise your body temperature, but not that much. To fix them, you just have to lower your body temperature through any means or apply reagents onto yourself via touch or just spray yourself with an extinguisher or stand under a shower. Cooling yourself through reagent exposure causes thermal shock though, which deals mild amounts of brute damage based on the volume of the reagent applied. You can make your reagents more effective (and thus more damage efficient) by cooling them before splashing them onto you, or using a reagent with a higher specific heat value (#37691). Current that is only plasma and the one new cooling reagent just for this wound. Also, chilled coolant spray bottles are mapped into robotics.

In terms of effects, burn wounds cause damage vulnerability on the robotic limb, flavored as heated metal becoming more malleable. They also slowly raise body temperature, but not to the extent of them actually becoming deadly unless you have like 4+ critical burns. Because they can't get infected, they're a lot less dangerous than organic wounds and combined with the fact that they cal cool off on their own you might as well just ignore them. I didn't really want to make them slowly kill you over time though so whatever, at least they matter in combat. 

**Blunt wounds** cause oscillation in the wound which forces you to stop or grasp the limb in order to not be knocked down or drop your stuff every couple of seconds when it starts vibrating. It also disables the limb like normal, making interactions with that limb slower. T3 fractures disable a limb entirely. T1 blunt wounds can be fixed via rng every time you're hit in that body part with a blunt attack (percussive maintenance) or just with a screwdriver and a couple seconds. The T2 is fixed with a screwdriver and then welder, but the screw driver step has a failure chance if you're doing it on yourself so you can use bone gel instead to glue the bodypart internals instead of fastening them (there is no glue item in ss13 afaik) or crowbar the part open completely, which deals some brute and disables the limb but lets you fix it with a screwdriver guaranteed. The failure chance is mitigated by wearing a diagnostic hud, having someone else treat you, or scanning the wound with a wound scanner. The T3 wound can only be fixed by having a very high body temperature or a burn wound on the broken limb to make the metal more malleable, and then prying it back into place with a crowbar. That downgrades it to a T2 blunt wound, which then still needs to be fixed with a screwdriver and finally a welder.

As for the actual effects, they are very similar to organic wounds in order to make them easily intuitable. Head fractures cause fracture-derived brain trauma, leg fractures cause limping, and chest fractures don't cause bleeding when attacked but instead cause brief stagger and confusion.

In terms of code you can make reagent containers spawn with chems at a different temp now, I had to add that for chilled coolant spray.

## Why It's Good For The Game

Adds more depth to robotic bodyparts. The wounds aren't even that bad.

changes.text: Added burn and blunt wounds for robotic bodyparts
Added a new reagent, a coolant for robotic burns.
Added chilled coolant spray (for robotic burn wounds) to robotics
removed magic strings from bone repair surgery required states text

title: 3 positive quirks / some minor quirk changes
author: MrMelbert
body:
## About The Pull Request

- Adds `Eccentric Correspondent`, 2 point positive quirk. Expands your mail list considerably to include items from any job, and then some. 
- Adds `Well Connected`, 6 point positive quirk. Grants you a discount on goodies and private orders from cargo, as well as on black market items. (And it has a sekret interaction as well)
- Adds `Shock Reflex`, 6 point positive quirk. Reduces the chance you get shocked when hacking vending machines or placing cables or the like. Does not effect chance to be shocked from bumping into shocked doors, for example.

- Removes some of the stranger mail goodies from a few quirks. 
   - Removed organ transport boxes from `Prosthetic Organ` and `Tin Man`
- Reduces chance of getting quirk mail from certain quirks that have stranger mail pools.
   - Affected quirks: Body Purist, Family Heirloom, Glass Jaw, Hemiplegic, Illiterate, Prosopagnosia, Pushover, Monochromatic, Pineapple hater, Pineapple Liker, Shifty Eyes, Vegetarian, Chipped, Freerunning, Jolly, Self Aware
- Increases chance of Gamer getting their mail

- Reduces quirk cost of throwing arm from 7 -> 5

## Why It's Good For The Game

- Quirks: A little more variety on the positive quirk front. Nothing super gamebreaking. 
   - `Eccentric Correspondent` allows people who love to pick up mail to gamble for wackier items. 
   - `Well Connected` is intended for people who have more "under-worldly" characters.
   - `Shock Reflex` is the one I expect most people to take - makes hacking a decent bit safer, but doesn't do anything to malf AIs. 

- Removed mail goodies: I just thought these were a bit out of place and useless. 

- Reduced chances: A lot of mail goodies are fitting, but are typically otherwise useless, especially if you end up getting multiple across one round. The reduced chances are intended to keep the flavor without replacing otherwise useful items.

- Increased gamer chance: I thought it fit.

- Throwing arm cost: 7 points for +2 range and "you never miss disposal bins" is frankly insane, particularly when comparing it to Spacer's 5 points or Strong Somach's 4 points.

body:
## About The Pull Request

Fixes #98438

My mistake was presuming that `view()` would include stuff visible to the client. However, that's not the case because `view()` fails when the mob is in contents. Ugh. I would have just barehanded did turf-turf checks, but that would regress the full point of #98395 (693797a6398775985ed7915d6b874885bdd63167). After trying MANY things, with none of them working (I have brain of peanut), there was only really one way I could reliably execute "is the client truly able to see that thing". This does leverage the `sight` flags we give to BYOND.

Note that this sort of thing does slightly revert the PR I did earlier, because the code itself knows that monkeys can use thermals/etc. in order to view objects as they might like to (TK+Thermal+Clever = 95, with Thermal being time-limited). I think that's where something like #98394 would have to be reopened to fix since there's no point adding more complexity to the TK check; would want to add limitations to ventcrawling. I really can't fathom a better way to do this to address that gap, but it at least improves the complexity of the overall issue while not adding a regression I didn't see coming.

Video for the fix.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5470221a-0ee1-4ddb-bcb9-511f96b0f047

## Why It's Good For The Game

I thought something would work the way I thought it would work, not the actual way it worked. Bleaugh. Learn something new every day.

title: Supermatter healing emitter beams have diminishing returns, but are (immediately) stronger
author: MrMelbert
body: ## About The Pull Request Supermatter healing emitter beams are roughly 5x stronger per beam (healing 1.2% integrity, up from 0.25%) However, they are now subject to diminishing returns: (numbers not necessarily final) After 18 beams, they lose 8% potency per additional hit, down to 0% potency at the 31st beam. This resets after 4 minutes of not being hit with a healing emitter beam. (Maths wise, this means you can heal roughly 25% of the SM's integrity before it bottoms out.) Reduced potency beams will cause periodic flashes around the crystal (blocked by sunglasses or better), as an indicator. 0% potency beams will travel through the crystal, and continue forward at a random angle (kinda funny imo). ## Why It's Good For The Game Healing emitter beams babyproof the Supermatter entirely, and it takes a lot of fun out of advanced setups. You can run practically any type of gas on the default setup so long as you keep adding more emitters. This PR seeks to shift their design intent slightly. Rather than add passive healing to the SM, they instead can act as burst healing in the event of emergency - If your SM's on fire because of an experiment gone wrong, you can flick the healing emitters on to buy you some time while you stabilize it, but they won't work forever. Some people might even think of cool circuit or assembly interactions with them, putting them on a timer or trigger. There's some neat sandbox potential there.

title: Tweals dynamic midround chances
author: MrMelbert
body:
## About The Pull Request

The old formula for determining if we should spawn a midround was
```dm
	var/chance = 0
	var/num_antags = length(GLOB.current_living_antags)
	var/num_dead = length(GLOB.dead_player_list)
	var/num_alive = get_active_player_count(afk_check = TRUE)
	if(num_dead + num_alive <= 0)
		return 0

	chance += 100 - (200 * (num_dead / (num_alive + num_dead)))
	if(num_antags < 0)
		chance += 50

	return chance
```
But there's 3 notable errors here
1. `if(num_antags < 0)`. This never happens, for obvious reasons
2. `var/num_alive = get_active_player_count(afk_check = TRUE)` Default argument has `alive_check = FALSE`, meaning this gets dead players, meaning this is (in practice) `var/num_players`.
3. `length(GLOB.dead_player_list)`. If you disconnect after you die, or take a ghost role, you no longer count as dead. 

New formula:
```dm
	var/total_crew = 0
	var/dead_or_mia = 0
	for(var/datum/mind/crew_mind as anything in get_crewmember_minds())
		if(isnull(crew_mind.current) || crew_mind.current.stat <= HARD_CRIT)
			dead_or_mia += 1
		total_crew += 1

	var/chance = 100 - (300 * (dead_or_mia / total_crew))
	if(length(GLOB.current_living_antags) <= 0)
		chance += 50

	return chance
```
Notable changes:
- It now counts all crewmembers who are alive or dead, rather than all players who are alive or dead. This means every crewmember who is dead slightly reduces the chance for midrounds to spawn, even if the player disconnects or takes a ghost role. 
   - Why: Dead crewmembers is more indicative of the status of the crew than dead players - otherwise, there's a funny phenomenon where a player dies, takes an antag role, and then the chance of antag spawning *goes up*. Likewise, if a nuke team gets wiped out, the chance of antag spawning *goes down*, since there's now a lot of ghosts hanging around. 
- the +50% chance if there are no living antags is properly factored in.   
   - Why: Bugfix. We want dynamic to spawn at least one antag if possible.
- the chance to add antags hits 0% when half the crew is dead, rather than the entire crew. 
   - Why: Before it literally required 100% of the server be dead to have the chance to spawn an antag hit 0%. Raising it to 50% (of the crew being dead) gives the other half of the crew a chance to escape. 
    
Other changes:
- Midround rulesets that require ghosts get set to zero weight if there are no ghosts. This means instead of picking a ruleset -> picks a ghost ruleset -> nothing happens, it will pick a ruleset that can actually execute.
   - Why: Sometimes, dynamic will have a lot of rulesets it wants to execute, but no ghosts to execute them with. This change **heavily** prioritizes stuff like Mass Traitor under the assumption that it will make more ghosts (to use on ghost rulesets later on).
   
Potential changes:
- Each living antag should be tracked for activity. If a supermajority of antags are inactive, chance goes up. ("activity" meaning actively antagonizing, not connected and playing.)
   - Why: If there is 1 traitor who hasn't done anything for 30 minutes, dynamic should guarantee a spawn. 
- Deaths too early into the round don't count towards reduced antag chance
   - Why: Prevent roundstart suicides from affecting antag chances throughout the round, realistically only deaths to antags should count (though tracking such a thing is infeasible).
- Rather than using chance, keep a running counter that goes up and down in response to certain events (such as an antag or crewmember dying) - then spawn an antag only if over a threshold and reset
    - Why: Because it's a probability, and it's checked every 5 minutes, it's gonna happen eventually. Let's say 10 people are dead on a 50 player round. After 15 minutes, that's a ~78% chance to spawn an antag. This is kind of hard to account for when balancing dynamic, so the thought is we could tie it to concrete events or progression milestones. 
  
## Why It's Good For The Game

This formula was totally broken which probably made dynamic a bit more unpredictable than it should've been
I'm also not confident in what exactly fixing it will do to dynamic. I know for certain there will be less antags on average for rounds with a lot of dead people, though.

changes.text: Dynamic has a significantly higher chance of spawning antags if there are no antags alive
Dynamic no longer counts dead people as alive for the purpose of antag spawn chance
Dynamic math changed slightly. Fewer antags are spawned if a significant amount of the crew is dead, and observers who were never part of the crew no longer reduce the chance of spawning antags.

Dynamic rulesets that a require ghosts cannot be picked if there are no ghosts. This means midround rulesets like Traitors / Mass Traitors will be significantly more common when there are no observers.

title: Removes excess filters from all SM setups, standardizes them a bit well
author: MrMelbert
body: ## About The Pull Request Removes the extra filters from the SM output on every map. Standardizes waste output on all maps to a design similar to that of Icebox and Delta, with a pressure valve leading out to space and a temperature valve leading into waste. Example (Metastation) Also took the opportunity to do stuff like clean up pipe runs, relocate vents/scrubbers into more convenient / balanced places, etc ## Why It's Good For The Game About a year ago I would against this change - I considered it to be soul - I figured people could find a use out of the extra filters - I'm against over-simplifaction / over-optimization of the default setup However over the past year I've come around on the idea - I still think it's soul, but it really does serve no purpose - I can't think of a use for them at all. Most people who add extra filters to speed up the rate that which it pumps air through rip them all up regardless. - I don't feel like removing them simplifies or optimizes the default setup in a major way And the benefits of doing it... - Easier for newer players. - For them, it's not at all obvious why the other filters even exist. - Nor is it obvious that failing to turn the three extra filters to "enabled, no filter" is *required* to avoid a later disaster. - Their main purpose ends up being a subtle way for the AI to sabotage the SM, which is something most newer players won't really know to check. - Clears up space, either for in round changes or mapping. (I used some of the extra space to standardize the setups a bit.) And why I standardized the outputs - I recognize that maps having unique facets gives them something that differentiates them (which is cool and good) but I'm on record stating the SM is like *the only* thing that shouldn't have major differences, due to its ability to explode and kill the round. (Birdshot proved that.) - Using the more niche components on a roundstart setup also helps teach people what they can be used for, which is neat.

Standardizes waste output of the Supermatter Engine across all maps

title: [READY] Nutimov: Selfish edition
author: Pumpkinoe
body:
## About The Pull Request

As an alternative to #98223, my PR that would have essentially turned nutimov into a more boring crewsimov, this PR aims to make Nutimov more interesting than the 'incredibly effective validhunter' lawset, changing a good portion of the laws to be slightly more selfish and in line with silicon policy, unlike the old laws.

## Why It's Good For The Game

This turns Nutimov from an incredibly safe validhunter lawset to a version that has the AI trying to prioritise keeping the crew alive to keep itself alive, a concept alluded to in the first line of nutimov but not expanded on. As soon as someone threatens the AI, they are no longer considered part of the nut and can be dealt with. Until then, anybody who is a part of the nut is given clemency, unless the AI deems attacks on the nutshell to be endangering the core.

It makes the AI slightly more selfish under Nutimov and gives it more of a chance to backfire if you don't treat the core right (thus making it a more interesting lawset, in my opinion).
